pageDescription: Manage reusable skills injected into digital employee system prompts
noPermission: No permission to access skill management
name: Name
nameHelp: kebab-case: lowercase letters/digits separated by single hyphens, e.g. weekly-report-format
nameInvalid: Must be kebab-case: lowercase letters and digits separated by single hyphens
descriptionPlaceholder: Use when the user asks for a weekly report; describes the required structure and tone...
descriptionHelp: Recommended "Use when ..." style so the model knows when to apply this skill; **also name the look-alike cases where it must not apply** — this is the text the model reads when deciding.
contentScaffoldHelp: Sections are yours to add or drop. Workflow: the steps. References: field meanings, terms and conventions written inline — the platform does not read external files. Guardrails: hard limits and failure handling. Triggering conditions belong in the description above, not repeated here. Any `...` placeholder you leave behind is injected into the model context verbatim, so delete them.
requiresHelp: Missing names only produce warnings on save; they never block
rejectedHint: The last review was rejected. Revise and resubmit.
diffLoadFailed: Failed to load comparison, please try again later
diffNoChanges: Draft is identical to the published version
diffDegradedNotice: Content too large: whole-line comparison only, no inline highlighting
diffKeyboardHint: Side-by-side comparison; press n for the next change, p for the previous one
execArtifactExcludeHelp: Artifacts matching these globs are not delivered to the user (no upload, no link) but still appear in the artifact manifest for troubleshooting. One per line, e.g. **/findings.json. Empty = deliver everything.
skillInUse: Skill "{name}" is bound to {count} digital employees. Unbind it first, or it cannot be deleted.
unbindWarning: The skill will no longer be injected into this digital employee's system prompt.
agentMdModeDesc: Who this digital employee is, what it does and the rules it follows all live in its role — edit it on the detail page
legacyDesc: This digital employee still uses the old prompt. After upgrading, its role and its skills are managed together, which is easier to follow (the model is still chosen in “AI model” above).
noAgentMdDesc: This digital employee has no role definition yet. Create one to describe who it is and what it does, and manage its skills in the same place (the model is still chosen in “AI model” above).
agentMdAlreadyExists: A role definition already exists; loaded the current version
wechatUpgradeDisabled: Wechat digital employees cannot use a role definition yet
agentMdHelp: Describe who this digital employee is, what it does and does not do, and how it should answer. Pick the model in “AI model” above — setting it here has no effect.
agentMdSaveFailed: Failed to save the role definition
agentMdSaveWarningsTitle: Saved, with {count, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}}
agentMdSaveWarningsHint: The text above now shows exactly what was saved.
exportViewNote: A read-only view the system assembles for you: the chosen model plus the skills, tools and knowledge bases this employee is bound to. Editing here is not saved — go back to the previous screen to make changes.
assetFilesDesc: Any skill can carry files, whether or not it is executable. Once published, text documents of kind "reference" can be read on demand by the model through skill_view — just write "see references/xxx.md" in the body instead of inlining the whole text. Scripts and binary material are only used inside the sandbox container of an executable skill.
assetReadableHint: Published text reference doc: the model can read it in full via skill_view. Mention this path in the body to point it there.
assetReadableAfterPublishHint: Draft assets are invisible to the model (not reviewed yet). The doc joins the model's readable list only after approval or self-publish.
assetKindHint: reference = a text document the model can read; for binary material (docx / pdf / xlsx / images) pick asset or data. The default is inferred from the directory and file extension and can be changed per file.
assetKindWarnBinaryAsReference: This looks like a binary file: marking it "reference" puts it on the model's readable list even though the model cannot decode it. Pick "asset" or "data" instead.
execAssetsDesc: Sandbox image, timeout and writable directories of an executable skill. Changes go back through review before they take effect at runtime.
execAssetsIdleDesc: This skill only carries documents, with no executable entry point. Make it executable when you need the model to run a script in the container; a knowledge-only skill never has to touch this.
assetExportAllHint: Download SKILL.md and every asset as a zip
assetDeleteWarning: This removes the draft asset only; the published snapshot is untouched until the next approval.
assetRevertNotice: This skill is published or rejected: any asset or runtime config change sends it back to draft.
assetRevertConfirmTitle: This sends the skill back to draft
assetRevertConfirmDesc: Asset and runtime config changes count as substantive edits. The skill returns to draft and must be resubmitted for review before it takes effect.
uploadDropzone: Drop files or a folder here
uploadHint: Up to {max} per file; kind defaults to what the top-level directory (scripts / data / assets) and file extension suggest, and can be changed per file before upload
uploadDone: {ok, plural, =1 {1 file uploaded} other {# files uploaded}}
pathErrorAbsolute: Path must be relative to the skill directory
pathErrorHiddenSegment: Paths cannot contain hidden files or directories starting with '.'; put persistent state directories under "writable subdirectories". The only exception is a root-level .env.example / .env.template (the key schema for personal env vars)
execImageHint: Only images registered in the platform allowlist can be used
execImageManual: Image allowlist unavailable — enter name:tag manually
execNeedsNetworkHint: Controls only whether this skill may reach the network, not what it does out there (there is no LLM-specific config any more). When off, the container has no network at all. Credentials for whatever it reaches are set by each user in their own environment variables — the platform never holds them.
execWarmPoolHint: Keeps the container alive in the warm pool after a run to speed up the next start
requiresToolsHelp: Pick from the tool pool a super admin has enabled globally. You can also type a name that is not online yet — it will be flagged until it exists.
requiresWorkflowsHelp: Tick this only when the skill needs a platform long task — ticking it makes the system tell the model how to start it. A skill that just describes steps the model performs itself does not need anything here. Globally disabled long tasks are not offered; one this skill already depended on before it was disabled still shows up, flagged, so you can decide whether to drop it.
requiresUnknownHint: {count, plural, one {# dependency is} other {# dependencies are}} not in the system yet (the name may be misspelled). The skill stays out of the system prompt until it exists.
requiresDisabledHint: Switched off globally — selecting it stops the skill from being injected
requiresOptionsUnavailable: The option list is unavailable right now; type dependency names manually.
requiresAllWorkflowsDisabled: Every long task in this deployment is globally disabled, so there is nothing to tick.
saveWarningsTitle: Saved, with {count, plural, one {# dependency warning} other {# dependency warnings}}
saveWarningsHint: These warnings never block saving, but a dependency that stays unresolved keeps this skill out of the system prompt at runtime.
diagnosticsAllEffective: {count, plural, one {# skill is in effect} other {All # skills are in effect}}
diagnosticsBlockedHint: A skill that is not in effect is never injected into this digital employee's system prompt. Resolve the gaps below to activate it.
diagnosticsReasonTools: Blocked first by its tool dependencies.
diagnosticsReasonWorkflows: Blocked first by its workflow dependencies.
gapToolNotFound: No such tool exists in the system — the name is probably misspelled. Correct the dependency in the skill editor.
gapToolGloballyDisabled: The tool exists but is disabled system-wide, so the name is fine. Ask a super admin to enable it.
gapToolNotBound: The tool is available and enabled; this digital employee just has not bound it yet. Bind it and the skill takes effect.
gapWorkflowNotRegistered: No workflow is registered under this kind — the name is probably misspelled. Correct the dependency in the skill editor.
gapWorkflowDisabled: The workflow kind is registered but switched off system-wide. Ask a super admin to enable it.
envDesc: Set the environment variables "{name}" needs. This configuration is yours alone — every user sets their own, and no review is involved; it takes effect as soon as you save.
envPrivacyNotice: Only you can see these values. An administrator can see which variable names you have set, never the values. The platform does not hold your credentials.
envTemplateSource: The variable list comes from this skill's {path} ({stage}). You can also add variables that are not on the list.
envEmpty: This skill declares no variables, and you have not added any of your own yet
envDeclaredUnset: Not set — the skill will not see this variable when it runs
envReplaceNotice: Saving replaces your whole configuration with what is in this table: removing a row deletes that variable, and clearing a value deletes it too.
envKeyErrorTooLong: A variable name cannot exceed 128 characters
envKeyErrorInvalid: Use only letters, digits and underscores, and do not start with a digit
envKeyErrorReserved: Names starting with SKILL_ are reserved by the platform (it uses SKILL_WORK_DIR and friends to tell the container where artifacts go) — pick another name
envValueErrorNul: A value cannot contain NUL characters
envErrorTooLarge: The variables cannot exceed 64 KB in total
bindSuccessWithTools: Skill bound; required tools added automatically: {tools}
author: Creator
managedHint: Maintained by the platform and updated with each release — cannot be edited or deleted. Copy it to build your own.
importHint: Drop a skill folder, a zip, or a single SKILL.md here
importStrippedRoot: Detected an extra top-level folder {root}; importing its contents as the root
importHasErrors: {n} problem(s) must be fixed first (marked red below)
importDisplayNameTip: Display name is left empty — fill it in on the edit page
importSingleMdNote: A lone SKILL.md is fine — document-only skills are common
importDetected: What you'll need to do after importing
importDetectedNone: No extra setup — ready to use once imported
importNeedsEnvDesc: A .env.example declaring these keys will be created; the actual values go in your personal environment variables — not into the skill, and not visible to anyone else
importNeedsNetworkDesc: SKILL.md makes curl / http calls. Granting egress is an authorization decision, so the import will not do it for you
importWillCreateExec: A run config will be created
importWillCreateExecDesc: Executable content detected — image {image}, 120s timeout, network off by default; adjustable later under Run config
filterDeptIncludesChildren: Selecting a department also shows skills from its sub-departments
scopeHint: Controls who can reuse this skill. Takes effect for others only after publishing.
scope_private_hint: Only you can see and use it
scope_dept_hint: Members of the owning department and all its sub-departments
scope_tenant_hint: All members of the same tenant
scope_public_hint: All members of all tenants (super admin only)
scopeOwnerDeptHint: Defaults to your own department. It decides where "and below" starts.
scopeOwnerDeptLocked: Owning department is fixed to yours
